Definition: properly, the same as the base of G5457 and G5316; to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say:--affirm, say. Compare G3004.
BiblicalUsage: Phemi means to say, to speak one's thoughts, and it carries some of the most famous sayings in the New Testament. Paul tells Festus he is not mad but speaks the words of truth and soberness, the blind man says Lord, I believe, and worships Him, and the prodigal comes to himself and says, I will arise and go to my father.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the verb is ordinary but the sayings are not: a sound mind, a new belief, and a son coming home all begin with one man saying the right words.
